title: Trace and coherence compatibilities of rational purity
statement:
The purity isomorphisms of
[thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] commute with the smooth trace of
[def-pur-smooth-trace] and with the composition and
base-change coherence.

proof.text: Fix the setting and the coefficient object of [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity], and an integral lattice presenting it. The rational categories of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] are defined on noetherian finite-dimensional schemes with $\ell$ invertible, and their lattices lie in the completed integral category. The schemes $X,Y$ involved are of finite type over the field $k$, hence noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied to their structure morphisms (a field is noetherian), and finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; $\ell$ is invertible on them since $\ell\ne p$. On these schemes [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] identifies that category with the derived-complete integral category used by reconstruction. Choose an interval $[a,b]$ bounding the first reduction of the lattice. Then [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] gives Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ for every reduction, so the lattice belongs to the required uniform finite-Tor domain. Put $F_h=Rh_!$, $G_h=Rh^!$, and $H_h=Lh^*(-)(d_h)[2d_h]$ for each smooth morphism involved. The integral isomorphisms are those of [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction], chosen as the simultaneous natural, scalar-compatible family of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality] used in rational purity. Reconstruction alone asserts no uniqueness of arbitrary coherent lifts, and no such uniqueness is used. Apply [prop-pur-adic-reconstruction-trace-coherence] to obtain the integral counit composite $t_{h,K}=\epsilon_{h,K}F_h(\gamma_{h,K})$, the transport of the formula of [def-pur-smooth-trace], and the integral versions of the equalities in [thm-pur-composition-coherence] and [thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence]. Thus at integral coefficients the single-map purity and its iterated composition agree, and the two paths around the smooth pullback square agree. These are supplied commutative diagrams, not consequences of detecting equality of morphisms by finite reductions.

Let $Q_E$ denote scalar localization. The general functor and natural-transformation assertion of [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] extends each supplied exact integral linear functor and its comparison transformations. The rational compact-support and exceptional functors are the coefficient-passage operations [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; [lem-coef-rational-operations] identifies their adjunction and preserves its units and counits. By [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity], $\gamma_{h,Q_EK}=Q_E(\gamma_{h,K})$. Therefore
$$Q_E(t_{h,K})=Q_E(\epsilon_{h,K})\,Q_EF_h(\gamma_{h,K})=\epsilon^E_{h,Q_EK}F^E_h(\gamma^E_{h,Q_EK})=t^E_{h,Q_EK}.$$
If the two integral paths in either coherence diagram are $r$ and $s$, Step 1 gives $r=s$, hence $Q_E(r)=Q_E(s)$. The functor equation $Q_E(ba)=Q_E(b)Q_E(a)$ identifies these with the paths in the rational diagram, using the extended comparison transformations. This proves both coherence assertions over E. Naturality also extends to every localized arrow $u/\varpi_E^j$: apply integral naturality to $u$ and multiply the equation by $\varpi_E^{-j}$. Thus changing a lattice by a rational isomorphism conjugates both paths by the same source and target identifications, and preserves their equality.

source.place: paragraph, E-reductions transported along the same exact functors

proof.text:
For a finite inclusion $E\subset L$, use the exact scalar extension $T=T_{L/E}$ of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Before rationalization write $C$ for the integral ordinary derived-tensor presentation. Use for $c$ the canonical natural comparison of [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison], on the finite-Tor domain checked in Step 1; it is the compact-support comparison named in the scalar-naturality helper. Write $a:CH_E\cong H_LC$, $b:CG_E\cong G_LC$, $c:CF_E\cong F_LC$ for the comparisons in [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality]. That statement gives $b_K C(\gamma_{E,K})=\gamma_{L,CK}a_K$ and specifies $b_K$ as the transpose of $C(\epsilon_{E,K})c_{G_EK}^{-1}$. The latter specification means
$$\epsilon_{L,CK}F_L(b_K)c_{G_EK}=C(\epsilon_{E,K}).$$
Naturality of $c$ at $\gamma_{E,K}$ now gives the explicitly typed trace equation
$$\begin{aligned}
C(t_{E,K})
&=C(\epsilon_{E,K})\,CF_E(\gamma_{E,K})\\
&=\epsilon_{L,CK}F_L(b_K)F_LC(\gamma_{E,K})c_{H_EK}\\
&=\epsilon_{L,CK}F_L(\gamma_{L,CK})F_L(a_K)c_{H_EK}\\
&=t_{L,CK}F_L(a_K)c_{H_EK}.
\end{aligned}$$
Rationalizing yields the same identity for $T$. It is the required coefficient compatibility of the trace, including its counit, rather than only compatibility of an isomorphism of its endpoints. The helper's unit, associator and shift equations ensure that the identifications used in this equation compose for a tower $E\subset L\subset M$. The unit, successive-extension and shift equations for $c$ itself come from [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison]. Consequently the comparison for the source $F_EH_E$ is $F_L(a_K)c_{H_EK}$ and is coherent in coefficient towers; the trace equation just proved is precisely its compatibility with the identity comparison on the target.

source.place: paragraph, Qbar-reductions transported along the same exact functors; counit calculation

proof.text:
In [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] an object is represented at a finite coefficient field and a morphism is represented over a common finite field. The higher-coefficient diagrams mean the transports prescribed by [def-pur-conventions]. Use [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] for the compatible operations and comparison transformations: its statement includes descent of compatible natural transformations and their equations. The scalar-compatible purity family and its inverses are supplied by [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]; the trace compatibility was proved in Step 3. The coherence comparisons also satisfy the required scalar equations. Indeed, write $\gamma^{\mathrm{it}}_{g,f,K}:H_{gf}K\to G_fG_gK$ for the iterated purity composite in the composition diagram of Steps 1–2, including its canonical pullback, twist and shift reassociations. Solving that diagram gives $c_{g,f}=\gamma^{\mathrm{it}}_{g,f}\gamma_{gf}^{-1}$. Writing $B_{\square}$ for the canonical left-hand pullback identification in the base-change square, solving its equality gives
$$\operatorname{Ex}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}_{f,v}=\gamma_{f',Lv^*(-)}B_{\square}(Lu^*\gamma_f)^{-1}.$$
Thus these actual coherence comparisons are composites of purity, its inverse and canonical pullback/twist comparisons. Their scalar compatibility follows by substitution from the purity equation of Step 3, the pullback comparisons and their composition/shift equations in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], and the scalar-extension twist convention [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. For composite transformations the verification is explicit: if $\beta_B T(\eta_E)=\eta_L\beta_A$ and $\beta_D T(\theta_E)=\theta_L\beta_B$, then
$$\beta_D T(\theta_E\eta_E)=\theta_L\beta_B T(\eta_E)=\theta_L\eta_L\beta_A;$$
for an isomorphism $\eta$, the first equation gives $\beta_A T(\eta_E^{-1})=\eta_L^{-1}\beta_B$ by multiplying by the inverses on the two sides. This proves compatibility for every path in the two diagrams.

For a path $r_E:A_EK\to B_EK$, the precise change-of-stage equation is therefore
$$T_{L/E}(r_E)=\beta_{B,L/E,K}^{-1}r_{L,T_{L/E}K}\beta_{A,L/E,K}.$$
The same source and target comparisons occur for the other path $s_E$. Step 2 gives $r_{L,TK}=s_{L,TK}$, so these representatives are equal. In a path with several arrows, inserting the displayed formula for each arrow cancels each intermediate $\beta\beta^{-1}$; the representative of its composite is exactly the displayed representative of the whole path. The unit and associator equations of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] and [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] make these representatives independent of enlargement. Hence the trace and both coherence equations descend for every object and every common-stage morphism, without a faithfulness assertion about reduction or scalar extension.

proof.text:
Finally check the source's direct-summand clause without adding a Karoubi envelope to the coefficient categories. The purity family preserves idempotent summands by [prop-pur-rational-purity-transitivity-summands]. If $i:K\to M$ and $p:M\to K$ split a summand, so $pi=1_K$, then for any natural transformation $\eta:A\Rightarrow B$ its summand component is
$$\eta_K=B(p)\eta_M A(i).$$
Indeed naturality at $i$ gives $\eta_M A(i)=B(i)\eta_K$, and postcomposing by $B(p)$ gives the formula. Apply this first to $\gamma$ and then to $t=\epsilon F(\gamma)$, which is natural because both $\gamma$ and the adjunction counit are natural, as in [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality] and [def-pur-smooth-trace]. Thus $t_K=p\,t_M FH(i)$ (the target functor of $t$ is the identity); this is exactly the restricted trace. If $r_M=s_M$ are the two paths of either already proved coherence diagram, multiplying by the common endpoint projections and inclusions gives $B(p)r_M A(i)=B(p)s_M A(i)$, the corresponding equality at the summand. Hence all trace and coherence identities survive the restriction referred to in the blueprint. The zero and identity projectors give respectively the zero restriction and the original identities.
